results.name: gif-correctness
notes: Real desktop BitBlt capture of a controlled 1280x720 animated pattern; SRCCOPY without CAPTUREBLT, full opaque GIF frames; delay accumulator uses actual capture-completion timestamps.
Before each sample, the harness reasserts HWND_TOPMOST without activation to keep its test pattern above ordinary topmost windows. A failed RGB sample is never retried.
Every captured frame matches the displayed source pattern; every decoded WIC frame is checked against its captured RGB hash. WIC validates decoding, not browser/Photos playback.

Harness costs are reported separately: pattern generation/painting, GdiFlush+DwmFlush presentation wait, RGB verification, and file writes. The drop count measures this complete sequential experiment, not a production recorder. Use the separate --spike-gif-pipeline experiment for throughput; these sequential timings cannot identify a production bottleneck.

P0 uses one UI/capture/encode thread and one pending compressed frame. P5 still needs parallel encoding, changed rectangles, transparency, cursor capture, backpressure, lock-screen pause, and preview UI. Wu fallback is unit-tested; this <=8-color workload exercises exact palettes.

Correctness-only experiment: source presentation is synchronized deliberately, and skipped scheduling ticks do not fail it. GIF timeline begins at first completed capture and ends at recording stop; it does not fabricate exposure before the first image exists.
This sequential correctness check has no throughput acceptance gate. Use these timings to budget P5 worker parallelism; preserved GIF duration does not hide dropped ticks.
